ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A long plank of mass $M$ is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A block of mass $m$ is placed on the left end of the plank. At a certain moment, they are given a velocity $v_{0}$ to the right. After some time, the long plank undergoes an elastic collision with a vertical barrier. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the long plank is $\mu$, and the gravitational acceleration is $g$.

1. If $M > m$ and the long plank is sufficiently long, what is the velocity of the slider when it becomes relatively stationary to the long plank again after the long plank collides with the vertical barrier?
2. In the case of the first question, what is the relative displacement between the slider and the long plank?
3. If $M < m$, what is the minimum length of the long board required to prevent the slider from falling off?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a small slider m is placed at the left end of a long wooden board M, and the two are on a smooth horizontal surface; there is a vertical baffle on the right side. The arrow v0 in the figure points to the right, indicating that initially the slider and the wooden board move to the right together, and the right end of the wooden board will first collide with the vertical baffle on the right side. Take rightward as the positive direction. Reasoning: After the wooden board undergoes an elastic collision with the fixed baffle, the wooden board's velocity reverses to -v0, while the slider is not subject to the baffle's impulse at the instant of collision and remains +v0. Therefore the initial relative sliding velocity after the collision is vrel,0 = v0 - (-v0) = 2v0. At this time the slider slides to the right relative to the wooden board, so the friction force on the slider is to the left and on the wooden board is to the right: am = -μg, aM = +μmg/M. 1. When M > m and the wooden board is long enough, during the sliding stage after hitting the wall, the horizontal momentum of the system composed of the slider and the wooden board is conserved. When relative rest is reached, the common velocity is u = (m v0 + M(-v0))/(M+m) = (m-M)v0/(M+m). Because M > m, the velocity direction is to the left; its speed is (M-m)v0/(M+m). 2. The relative acceleration is arel = am - aM = -μg - μmg/M = -μg(1+m/M). The relative velocity decreases from 2v0 to 0, so the magnitude of the relative displacement is s = (2v0)^2 / [2 μg(1+m/M)] = 2M v0^2/[μ(M+m)g]. 3. When M < m, the common velocity after the first sliding to relative rest is u = (m-M)v0/(M+m), which is positive, that is, it still moves to the right, toward the right-side baffle in the figure, so the wooden board will elastically collide with the baffle again and relative sliding will occur repeatedly. The baffle collision is elastic and the ground is smooth, so mechanical energy is lost only because of work done by friction between the slider and the wooden board. In the critical case of not falling off, the wooden board length equals the cumulative relative sliding distance Lmin in the whole process. Finally, all the initial total kinetic energy is dissipated by friction: μmg Lmin = (1/2)(M+m)v0^2, so Lmin = (M+m)v0^2/(2μmg).
